title: Streaming SSE chunking/backpressure debug notes
content:
Context:
Quick notes and breadcrumbs while chasing intermittent broken SSE streams from the hosted API. Symptoms: client receives an initial event or a few small chunks then stalls indefinitely (no "event: message" after), or chunks arrive but are aggregated oddly by intermediaries and client-side backpressure causes very high latency. Repro is flaky locally but reproducible against the staging cluster when under load.

Timeline / quick hits:
- 2025-02-14 09:30: First noticed via e2e (playwright) tests that read stream hung ~30s into response for ~10% of runs.
- 2025-02-15 11:12: Reproduced manually with heavy concurrency by spinning 50 curl clients.
- 2025-02-16 16:40: Suspected NGINX/proxy buffering or gzip interfering with chunked streaming.
- 2025-02-17 09:05: Tried disabling compression and proxy_buffering in ingress  partial improvement.

Repro commands (use these to reproduce locally / against staging):
1) Raw curl to mimic a simple event-stream client (no buffering):
   curl --no-buffer -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
     -X POST 'https://staging-api.redwood.local/v1/streams/chat?stream=true' \
     -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-lite","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"stream me a long response"}]}'

   Notes: --no-buffer disables libcurl buffering. Observe raw chunk boundaries in terminal.

2) Multiple concurrent clients (flaky reproducer):
   for i in {1..50}; do curl --no-buffer -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
     -X POST 'https://staging-api.redwood.local/v1/streams/chat?stream=true' \
     -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-lite","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"send ~200 lines\"}]}' & done; wait

3) Node minimal client using fetch + text decoder stream (to observe backpressure):
   // run with node 18+
   const res = await fetch('https://staging-api.redwood.local/v1/streams/chat?stream=true', {
     method: 'POST',
     headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${TOKEN}`, 'Accept': 'text/event-stream', 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
     body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'redwood-chat-lite', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'stream long' }] })
   })
   const reader = res.body.getReader();
   while (true) {
     const { done, value } = await reader.read();
     if (done) break;
     const chunk = new TextDecoder().decode(value);
     console.log('CHUNK:> ' + chunk.replace(/\n/g, '\\n'));
     // artificially slow consumer to simulate backpressure
     await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 150));
   }

Observed outputs / error snippets:
- server sends initial comment + data then nothing:
  : ping
  id: 1
  data: {partial...}
  
  <client stalls, no further data for 30s>

- sometimes curl shows chunk boundaries like: 
  [0K
  23
  event: message
  data: ...
  
  0
  
  then connection stays open.

- Node client sometimes receives a giant aggregated chunk (many events merged) or receives very small fragments (single-byte chunks), both problematic for our parser.

Hypotheses:
- Proxy/nginx ingress is buffering or re-chunking response, causing large gaps (proxy_buffering, gzip, or chunked transfer coalescing).
- Our runtime does not flush small writes promptly (missing flush call or stream.write semantics on the worker).
- TLS / ALPN buffering in the LB under high concurrency introduces head-of-line delays.
- HTTP/2 -> HTTP/1.1 conversion in front-proxy affects chunking semantics (some proxies buffer HTTP/2 until threshold).
- Consumer backpressure  our server continues to produce but client slow consumption leads to TCP receive window exhaustion and OS-level stall.

Experiments performed (and results):
1) Disable gzip on upstream + ingress:
   - set gzip off at ingress and upstream in staging. Result: slightly fewer aggregated chunks, but stalls still happen.
2) Set proxy_buffering off in nginx ingress:
   - added proxy_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1; chunked_transfer_encoding on.
   Result: improved, fewer stalls, but not eliminated under 50 concurrent clients.
3) Force small flushes on the serving runtime (explicit wrtie+flush after each event):
   - added an explicit flush after writing each event in the runtime. Result: reduced incidence of huge aggregated chunks; latency improved for some runs.
4) Tried curl with and without --no-buffer:
   - with --no-buffer we see event boundaries more clearly, without it curl sometimes shows aggregated output.
5) Reproduced using socat to inspect raw TCP stream between LB and service:
   - observed bursty arrival pattern: multiple small writes from process -> aggregated by LB and sent in bursts.

Key config knobs to investigate in infra:
- nginx ingress: proxy_buffering, proxy_max_temp_file_size, proxy_http_version, proxy_set_header Connection '', chunked_transfer_encoding.
- LB (envoy/traefik): http2->http1 bridge settings, max buffering, stream timeouts.
- TLS termination: does termination happen at LB or ingress? buffering observed when TLS at external LB.

Temporary mitigations applied:
- Set proxy_buffering off for streaming routes in staging.
- Add server-side pacing: small sleep (1-2ms) between event writes to avoid bursts (temporary, hacky).

Things to try next / TODOs:
- Add instrumentation: per-request write syscall timestamps (or trace bytes-per-write) to see if server is coalescing writes.
- Verify HTTP/2 path: test client via curl --http2-prior-knowledge vs forced HTTP/1.1 to compare behavior.
- Try running the runtime behind a raw TCP proxy (no HTTP buffering) to verify whether buffering is introduced by HTTP proxies.
- Run a controlled test: single producer, single slow consumer (simulate slow read) to see if TCP window/clogging is server or client caused.
- Add server-side SSE keepalive comment every 10s to detect live stalls vs connection drop.

Notes for upstream runtime changes (ideas):
- Ensure runtime uses chunked transfer encoding and calls flush after each SSE block.
- Batch writes into reasonably sized chunks, but ensure a minimum flush frequency (e.g., no more than 200ms without flush).
- Expose config to disable internal write coalescing for streaming endpoints.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why does disabling proxy_buffering only partially help? (maybe LB-level buffering still in path)
- Is gzip/deflate compression on path incompatible with incremental streaming on current proxy stack?
- Do we need to change the API contract to recommend clients use streaming parsers tolerant to chunk boundaries? (we already do, but need examples)

Quick checklist for PR/changes:
- [ ] Add test harness for streaming under load (50-100 concurrent) that asserts no >5s stall between events.
- [ ] Add small write instrumentation to runtime and log sample sizes.
- [ ] Add SSE keepalive comment every 10s in runtime.
- [ ] Update docs / examples to show best-effort client code (use --no-buffer, Node reader with small timeouts).

Random breadcrumbs / snippets saved here: 
- curl --no-buffer shows boundaries when proxy not buffering.
- Node + setTimeout(150) reliably triggers slow consumer case.
- Proxy buffer off + runtime flush + small pacing = current best config in staging.

If you pick this up: start by re-running the concurrent curl loop against staging and toggle ingress proxy_buffering; capture tcpdump between ingress and pod to confirm where aggregation happens.

-- Isaac
